players.product: AI cluster design/integration & managed services (plus Smart Modular memory)

quarterly_data.signal: CXL and MemoryAI: CEO says bookings and pipeline for the CXL memory expansion products continue to strengthen. As proof points, in Q4 Penguin secured business with a leading global AI server manufacturer (unnamed) whose platforms support large-scale AI training and inference - a win the CEO said reinforces the strength of its memory portfolio for data center AI infrastructure (the call does not say it is a CXL product) - and expanded its relationship with a leading next-generation AI infrastructure inference provider (unnamed) rapidly scaling inference deployments with Penguin's CXL memory expansion cards. The cards are primarily for inference workloads and 'we see this CXL business taking off very strongly'. Penguin is also developing a CXL AIC product line designed to repurpose installed DDR4 memory for AI infrastructure, and its MemoryAI roadmap extends to future memory appliances including photonic high-bandwidth memory solutions to expand GPU memory capacity and bandwidth.

Interim CFO Aaron Johnson: Q4 gross sales were $1.57 billion and gross cost of goods sold was $1.42 billion (the basis for DSO, DPO and inventory days); the difference between gross and net sales relates primarily to the memory business' logistics services, which are accounted for on an agent basis.
quarterly_data.figure: Gross sales $1.57 billion; gross cost of goods sold $1.42 billion (Q4 FY2026)
